2026-12-20.title: Fourth Sunday of Advent
readings: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever
For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord
The mystery kept secret for long ages is now disclosed
You will conceive in your womb and bear a son
2026-12-20.alt: Year B. Liturgical colour: violet. O Antiphon of the day: O Key of David.
2026-12-20.verse: Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
theo: On the last Sunday of Advent the readings bring two houses face to face. King David, settled in his cedar palace, wants to build a house for the ark of God. Through Nathan, God turns the offer around: “Are you the one to build me a house to live in?… the LORD will make you a house.” God promises David a dynasty, an heir whose throne “shall be established forever”. David wanted to give God a house; God gives David a house, a family line, a future.

In Nazareth the angel Gabriel tells Mary that the promise to David is now fulfilled: her son “will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give to him the throne of his ancestor David. He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” The everlasting house God promised is not made of cedar but of flesh: the Son of God will dwell in the womb of a virgin. Mary herself becomes the house of God, the Ark of the New Covenant.

Mary's question, “How can this be, since I am a virgin?”, is not doubt but a request for understanding. The answer is the Holy Spirit and the power of the Most High overshadowing her, the same verb used of the cloud over the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). The Church professes that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary (CCC 484–486). And Mary gives her free consent: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” Paul calls this “the mystery that was kept secret for long ages but is now disclosed”, made known to all nations to bring about “the obedience of faith”.
conn: In Hebrew bayit means both a building and a dynasty. God refuses David's building but promises him a dynasty (2 Samuel 7:11, 16). The wordplay runs through the whole chapter.
Luke 1:35 uses episkiazō, the word used in the Greek Old Testament for the cloud of God's glory resting on the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). Mary becomes the new dwelling of God.
The Ark of the New Covenant.
The Fathers saw in Mary the true Ark: the old ark carried the tablets of the Law, manna and Aaron's rod; Mary carries the Word, the Bread of Life and the true Priest.
Today's O Antiphon: “O Key of David and sceptre of the house of Israel, who open and no one shuts: come and lead the prisoners from the prison house” (cf. Isaiah 22:22).
Paul's phrase (Romans 16:26; 1:5) is exactly what Mary lives at the Annunciation: obedience that comes from faith (CCC 144, 148).
An unimportant village not mentioned in the Old Testament. God's greatest promise is fulfilled in an obscure place, to a young woman nobody had heard of.
altar: At every Mass, in the Creed, we bow at the words “and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man”. On Christmas and the Annunciation we kneel.
As Mary received the Word in her womb, we receive the Word made flesh in Communion. Her “let it be with me” is the model of every “Amen” we say before receiving the Body of Christ.
outline: Ask: have you ever wanted to do something great for God, and found that God wanted to do something greater for you?

fathers: In his famous homily he imagines the whole world waiting for Mary's answer: “Answer quickly, O Virgin. Speak the word, and receive the Word.”
“The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary.”
He says Mary conceived Christ first in her heart by faith before conceiving him in her womb.
magis: Conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary.
Mary's fiat: the obedience of faith.
Mary, not merely passive, cooperated freely in salvation.

2026-12-20.prayer: Pour forth, we beseech you, O Lord, your grace into our hearts, that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ your Son was made known by the message of an Angel, may by his Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

illus: In Kerala, when a family builds a new house, the first thing placed inside is often a picture of the Holy Family or the Sacred Heart. David wanted to build God a house; God wanted to live in ours.

family.explain: The angel Gabriel asked Mary to be the mother of Jesus. Mary said yes to God. In a few days we will celebrate the birth of her Son.
family.intention: We pray to say yes to God like Mary.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family make room for Jesus this Christmas?”

kidsaint: A Jesuit priest who wrote simple catechisms so children could learn their faith. Lesson: learning about God helps us love him.
term: The announcement by the angel Gabriel to Mary that she would conceive the Son of God by the Holy Spirit (Luke 1:26–38).

pm.open: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. Lord God, on this last Sunday of Advent, give us Mary's faith to say yes to your word. Amen.
share: David wanted to build God a house, but God promised to build David a house (2 Samuel 7:11). How has God done more for me than I could do for him?
Mary asked: how can this be? (Luke 1:34). What question do I bring to God?
Mary said: let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). Where must I say yes?
pm.resp: Let it be done to us according to your word.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may welcome God's word.
For expectant mothers, that they may be safe and joyful.
For the homeless, that God may provide them a house.
For all who find God's will hard to accept.
For our families, as we prepare for Christmas.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose the Virgin Mary to be the Mother of your Son. With her, we say: here we are, the servants of the Lord. Let it be done to us according to your word. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Christmas, the readings tell us about two houses.

King David lived in a palace of cedar. He looked at the ark of God in a tent and felt ashamed: “I live in luxury and God lives in a tent. Let me build God a house.” A good thought. But God answers through the prophet Nathan: “You will build me a house? No, I will build you a house.” God promises David a family line whose throne will last forever.

A thousand years later, in a small village called Nazareth, the angel Gabriel greets a young woman: “You will conceive and bear a son… The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” The promise to David comes true, not in a palace but in a girl's humble home.

Mary asks, “How can this be?” Not doubt, but faith seeking to understand. The angel answers: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.” Just as God's cloud rested on the tent in the desert, God now rests on Mary. She becomes the house of God, the true Ark of the Covenant.

And then her answer: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” With these words, the whole history of salvation turns. St Bernard imagined the whole world holding its breath, waiting for her yes.

Like David, we often want to do great things for God. But God wants first to do great things in us. This Christmas, he asks to make his home in our hearts. Let us make room, like Mary, and say: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
kids: Children, King David wanted to build a big house for God. But God said: I will build a house for you!
Then God chose Mary to be the mother of Jesus. Mary said yes to God.
Jesus wants to live in our hearts too. Can we say yes like Mary?
This week, help set up the crib at home, and leave the manger empty until Christmas night!
